A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HARPO and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results on ReDial, INSPIRED, and MUSE, component ablations, human evaluations, and cross-domain transfer results (Tables 3, 4, 8, and 9).

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, human-evaluation, transfer, and supplementary analysis results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The STAR, CHARM, BRIDGE, MAVEN, and VTO components and four-stage training procedure are retained. v2 specifies the already-mentioned adaptive margin and explains implementation details without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use ReDial and INSPIRED for movie recommendation and MUSE for fashion recommendation, including the same movie–fashion transfer scenarios. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership and descriptions remain unchanged in the benchmark, generation, human-evaluation, and transfer comparisons. DCRS receives a different citation, but its description and result rows remain unchanged; no different evaluated implementation is documented.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, preprocessing, metrics, 99-negative ranking protocol, model configurations, training budgets, and human-evaluation sample sizes remain unchanged (Table 2 and Appendices C, D, and F).

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same component, mechanism, and training-stage ablations; transfer and hyperparameter studies; reasoning and computational analyses; and error analysis. Appendix E's reward-dimension and preference-data-quality findings are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report three runs with seeds 42, 123, and 456, mean ± standard deviation, Bonferroni-corrected paired t-tests, and Mann–Whitney tests for human evaluation. Correlation and annotator-agreement reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All 13 table bodies match, and the reported textual findings are retained. For example, HARPO's Table 3 R@10 remains 29.8% on ReDial, 27.4% on INSPIRED, and 38.6% on MUSE.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 newly defines the adaptive margin as m = m0 + 0.5 sigmoid(Wm[h+;h−]); v1 only described it as adaptive. This adds a mathematical specification. Other equations are retained or renumbered, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The shortened abstract preserves the claims about quality-oriented recommendation, hierarchical preferences, deliberative reasoning, and benchmark improvements. The introduction's contributions and conclusion retain their original meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component contributions and transfer remain unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same qualifications concerning reward-model circularity, human-evaluation scale, backbone fairness, caption-based visual inputs, domain coverage, and computational overhead.

D1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.5 newly specify projection dimensions, the adaptive-margin formula, the linear VTO head, and several component variables. Appendix D.3 replaces the anonymous code link with a project-page link and explicitly lists datasets among available resources; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds discussion of static multimodal recommendation through Raj et al. (2023, 2025) and Mondal et al. (2023), distinguishing it from conversational preference revelation. Dao et al. (2024) and Wei et al. (2025) replace earlier retrieval and multimodal citations. The overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract, expands explanatory clauses around method equations, revises affiliations and bibliographic text, and adjusts VTO terminology. The section hierarchy and overall narrative organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Both embedded figures are identical, and all tables retain their structure and contents. Previously inline equations become numbered displays, text and table placements shift, and limited caption edits include the updated equation reference in Table 4.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical clarity by defining the previously unspecified adaptive margin and explaining parameter dimensions and component symbols. The shorter abstract and focused related-work expansion also improve readability and context. Empirical evidence and substantive evaluation limitations remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
